_comment: Metadata only: no exposure data ships with spacescans. Each site downloads the data into its own data directory. 'artifacts' are files on the project mirror (sha256 + byte counts are the published SHA256SUMS.txt values); 'datasets' are what the pipeline reads under the data root; 'variables' maps each catalog variable to the datasets it needs. Validated against manifest.schema.json.

iu-onedrive.label: SPACESCANS project mirror (IU OneDrive folder Documents/spacescans-pipeline-data)
iu-onedrive.note: Anonymous 'anyone with the link' share. Files are read through _layouts/15/download.aspx?SourceUrl=<folder>/<name>, which honours HTTP Range (206 verified 2026-10-12 14:59 EDT); the _api/web/GetFileByServerRelativeUrl(...)/$value endpoint used by the web's fetch_distribution.sh ignores Range.

nhd_features_cache_v1.tar.gz.note: Needs about 89 GB free while unpacking (archive plus extracted tree).

vnl.title: VIIRS Nighttime Lights, VNL v2.1 annual average_masked, 2013-2019
vnl.provider: Earth Observation Group (EOG), Payne Institute for Public Policy, Colorado School of Mines
vnl.license: CC BY 4.0, per EOG's licence document
vnl.redistribution: allowed with attribution (CC BY 4.0); earlier project notes saying VNL may not be redistributed are superseded by EOG's licence
vnl.attribution: Credit the Earth Observation Group, Payne Institute for Public Policy, Colorado School of Mines, as the EOG licence requires, and cite Elvidge et al. 2021, Remote Sensing 13(5):922, for annual VNL v2.

terms.summary: Free EOG account required to download. Use and redistribution are allowed under CC BY 4.0 with attribution to EOG.

instructions: Create a free EOG account at https://eogdata.mines.edu/products/vnl/ and sign in (spacescans does not automate the login).

Download the annual global VNL v2.1 'average_masked' file for each year 2013-2019: VNL_v21_npp_{year}_global_vcmcfg_c202205302300.average_masked.dat.tif.gz for 2013 and VNL_v21_npp_{year}_global_vcmslcfg_c202205302300.average_masked.dat.tif.gz for 2014-2019.
gunzip each file and place the .tif files, with their original names, in <data_dir>/VNL/C3/. Keep exactly one file per year: the reader reads every *.tif in that folder.
Each unpacked file is about 11.6 GB (about 81 GB for the 7 years).

temis_uv_raw.title: KNMI TEMIS daily UV (uvief, uvdec, uvdvc, uvddc), raw HDF4 files, 2013-2019
temis_uv_raw.provider: KNMI / ESA, Tropospheric Emission Monitoring Internet Service (TEMIS)
temis_uv_raw.license: Free use with credits; redistribution not granted
temis_uv_raw.redistribution: not granted: neither the raw HDF files nor the converted parquet may be redistributed; every site downloads and converts its own copy

terms.license: TEMIS data policy (credit KNMI/ESA); no redistribution grant
terms.summary: Download from KNMI yourself; do not share the files or values derived from them without KNMI's permission.

instructions: spacescans data fetch --dataset temis_uv_raw --accept-terms knmi-temis downloads them for you (one file at a time from KNMI's CloudFront mirror; already present days are skipped). Or by hand:

Download the daily files {var}YYYYMMDD.hdf for var in uvief, uvdec, uvdvc, uvddc and the years 2013-2019 (about 10,220 files, about 31.6 GB) from the KNMI archive; the mirror https://d1qb6yzwaaq4he.cloudfront.net/uvradiation/v2.0/{year}/{mm}/{var}YYYYMMDD.hdf serves the same files.
Place them as <data_dir>/TEMIS/C4/raw/{var}/{year}/{var}YYYYMMDD.hdf.
2016-02-29 is missing upstream for all four variables; that gap is expected.
Reading needs the hdf4 extra (pyhdf). The first run converts the files to <data_dir>/TEMIS/C4/converted/, so the data directory must be writable then.

download.note: KNMI's CloudFront distribution of the TEMIS UV archive v2.0; Range is honoured.

temis_uv_converted.title: KNMI TEMIS daily UV converted to parquet (produced locally from temis_uv_raw)
temis_uv_converted.provider: Generated on this machine by the TEMIS reader (spacescans.tools.temis_convert) from temis_uv_raw
temis_uv_converted.license: Derived from TEMIS; redistribution not granted
instructions: Produced automatically by the first TEMIS run (about 2 minutes) from the raw HDF files; nothing to download.

acag.title: ACAG V5.NA.05 / V5.NA.05.02 surface PM2.5 and composition, biweekly 0.01 degree NetCDF, 2013-2019 (plain and FromBiomass)
acag.provider: Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group (ACAG), Washington University in St. Louis
acag.license: Not stated for the North American V5.NA.05 product; ACAG states CC BY 4.0 for its global product only
acag.redistribution: not confirmed for this product: do not redistribute until ACAG confirms the licence; every site downloads its own copy
acag.attribution: Cite the van Donkelaar et al. paper that the ACAG dataset page lists for V5.NA.05 / V5.NA.05.02.

terms.license: see the ACAG dataset page; CC BY 4.0 is stated for the global product only
terms.summary: Download from WashU ACAG yourself and cite the product paper. Do not redistribute the North American files.

instructions: spacescans data fetch --dataset acag --accept-terms acag-v5na05 downloads them for you from the four WashU Box shares, one file at a time; already present files are skipped. Or by hand:

From the ACAG surface PM2.5 page, download V5.NA.05 (total PM2.5) and V5.NA.05.02 (BC, DUST, NH4, NO3, OM, SO4, SS), biweekly NetCDF, years 2013-2019, each in the plain and the FromBiomass variant: 16 folders x 182 files = 2,912 files, about 27.4 GB.
The four WashU Box shares do not allow folder downloads; files are fetched one by one (spacescans-web pipeline-data/ACAG/README.md lists the share IDs and the method).

Place plain files in <data_dir>/ACAG/C4/xNorthAmerica/{SPECIES}/BiWeekly/ and FromBiomass files in <data_dir>/ACAG/C4/xNorthAmerica/{SPECIES}_bm/BiWeekly/, SPECIES in PM25, BC, DUST, NH4, NO3, OM, SO4, SS; spacescans data import acag <files or folders> sorts them by name.
Reading needs the nc extra (xarray, netCDF4).

download.note: Box's folder API rejects anonymous calls and folder download is disabled: each folder's HTML page is paged with ?page=N and files are fetched one by one via index.php?rm=box_download_shared_file. Every listed .nc is routed by the import rule; other years are skipped.

faqsd.title: US EPA FAQSD daily ozone (8-hour maximum) and PM2.5 (daily average) by 2010 census tract, 2013-2019
faqsd.provider: US EPA, Fused Air Quality Surfaces Using Downscaling (FAQSD), via RSIG
faqsd.attribution: Credit the US EPA (FAQSD downscaler outputs, RSIG).

terms.summary: Public domain. Downloads come from EPA's server, which does not support resuming and streams at about 0.25 MB/s.

instructions: spacescans data fetch --dataset faqsd --accept-terms epa-faqsd downloads them for you: one unbroken connection per file (no overall time cap), size and gzip checks, then gunzip into place; already present files are skipped. Or by hand:
Download https://ofmpub.epa.gov/rsig/rsigserver?data/FAQSD/outputs/{year}_{kind}.txt.gz for year 2013-2019 and kind ozone_daily_8hour_maximum, pm25_daily_average (14 files, about 6.5 GB compressed).
EPA's server ignores Range requests and streams at about 0.25 MB/s, so each 470 MB file needs one unbroken connection of about 30 minutes; never cap a download below about 3 hours.
gunzip each file into <data_dir>/FAQSD/C4/{year}_{kind}.txt and keep the names exactly as published (about 23.3 GB unpacked).

download.note: EPA's rsigserver ignores Range and streams at about 0.25 MB/s: every attempt starts from byte 0 on one long connection. reference_download_bytes are the Content-Length values seen on 2026-09-15.
